note: Content per GW, supplier shares and absorption rates are Claude estimates, calibrated so share × content × ~18 GW of global AI capacity a year roughly matches each company’s data center revenue; revenue run-rates are the latest quarter ×4 (Nvidia FQ3 $115.8B, Applied Materials FQ4 $10.41B, Vertiv Q3 $4.31B, GE Vernova Q3 $12.6B, Constellation Q3 $9.55B; ~ = estimate). Shares that don’t add to 100% go to an “Other suppliers” bucket. Updated with the daily US data center risk task.

cats.why: Supply is capped by CoWoS packaging and HBM, so a delayed US campus mostly frees allocation for other buyers (sovereign AI, Middle East, Asia) rather than cutting shipments.
Head-node and general compute CPUs are less supply-constrained, so lost US racks are only partly re-sold.
Memory is sold out into 2027 at record margins; delayed demand is instantly re-allocated, so the hit shows up as slightly less pricing power, not lower volume.
NAND is tight too, but more exposed to the timing of US storage build-outs.
Ethernet and NVLink switching is bought with each cluster; less absorbed than GPUs because it is designed per site.
EML/CW laser supply is tight (indium phosphide capacity), so part of the demand is absorbed, but transceiver orders follow cluster go-lives closely.
Fiber and cabling are installed on site, so a delayed campus delays the order almost one for one.
Wafers and CoWoS slots are booked a year ahead and re-assigned to other chip customers.
Second derivative: tool orders depend on fab expansion plans, which a 12-month US slip barely moves; test (Teradyne) is closer to unit volumes.

Switchgear, UPS, chillers and liquid cooling are site-specific and ship with construction, so they are the most directly exposed to US delays; 12–18 month backlogs and global customers absorb part of it.
Annual energy sales per GW of load (~8 TWh at ~$65/MWh, the middle of EIA’s $47–85/MWh range for ERCOT North in 2027); a delayed Texas campus is load a Texas generator does not get.

views.NVDA: Largest dollars deferred, smallest real damage from state policy: Nvidia is supply-capped and re-routes allocation. FQ3 settled the demand question for now: data center revenue $107.6B (+110%), Q4 guided to $130B, ~75% growth guided for FY2028, B300 prices up 60%+ since launch and a $2.5T cloud backlog, so the SemiAnalysis cut and post-Huang selloff look like sentiment. Its GPU share here moves to 80% to match the ~$430B data center run-rate; the risk to watch is customer financing, which Kress now limits to selective land/power/shell support.
views.AMD: Exposed through MI-series GPUs and EPYC CPUs, with OpenAI (Stargate) ties putting more of its 2027 ramp in Texas than peers. SemiAnalysis's cut fell mostly on Nvidia, and TensorWave signed a six-year, 457 MW MI455X deal with OpenAI on Nov 16, yet the stock fell 5.6% to $504 with the export-rule selloff; that is sector sentiment, and the per-GW content assumption is unchanged.
views.AVGO: Custom ASIC (Google TPU, Meta, OpenAI) plus Tomahawk switching. Google's and Meta's Texas plans touch two of its biggest XPU customers, but expect deferrals of quarters, not cancellations. The 4.8% fall on Nov 13 (Redburn downgrade) unwound part of the post-Huang rotation into custom silicon; no change to content or share.
views.MRVL: Small absolute exposure but high operating leverage; AWS Trainium and optical DSP volumes follow US cluster go-lives closely.
views.ARM: Royalty per CPU is small, so direct impact is negligible. The 8.1% fall on Nov 16 reflects its tie to Nvidia's Vera CPU and SemiAnalysis's Nvidia-heavy forecast cut, plus SoftBank's Stargate financing; it is sentiment rather than lost data center volume.
views.INTC: Server CPU recovery is tied to general cloud builds more than giant AI campuses, so the hit is modest; foundry ambitions do not depend on US data center siting.
views.SKHY: HBM is sold out: long-term deals cover over half of 2027–28 capacity and module makers see the tightest stretch through Q2 2027. SemiAnalysis's 30% cut to 2028 HBM demand (Nov 16) and the antitrust suit are the risks to watch; they threaten 2028 pricing talks more than contracted 2027 volume, so the absorb rate is unchanged.
views.MU: Same as SK hynix on HBM, with more US-centric enterprise SSD and DRAM module exposure. Near-term pricing is still tight (TrendForce sees Q4 DRAM contracts up 10–15%), but SemiAnalysis cut its 2028 HBM demand forecast 30%, which is the first credible hit to the out-year volume story, and the DRAM antitrust suit is proceeding. The 7.6% drop to $719 on Nov 16 prices 2028 risk; 2027 volumes and shares here are unchanged.
views.SNDK: Datacenter is now 44% of sales and enterprise SSDs ship with each campus, so it carries more timing risk than the HBM makers. Memory makers are reportedly lining up new enterprise price hikes, but the stock fell 5.6% on Nov 13 with the chip unwind; that is sentiment, not lost orders.
views.COHR: Transceivers and lasers ship close to cluster go-live, so a Texas pause shifts revenue right. But data center revenue is up 85% with 60%+ growth guided, and the administration pressing ahead on curbs for new Chinese transceiver models (China is ~2/3 of supply) lifted it ~10% on Nov 17: share gain from a ban outweighs any US delay, with indium phosphide retaliation the main risk.
views.LITE: High exposure per dollar of revenue: EML and CW lasers for 800G/1.6T are tied to new clusters. The tight laser market cushions price, not timing. The administration now plans to press ahead with curbs on new Chinese transceivers despite hyperscaler lobbying (+8% on Nov 17), which would shift share to US-sourced optics, though China could retaliate on indium phosphide.
views.AAOI: Most exposed optics name relative to size; depends on a few hyperscaler programs, some in Texas. It is also the clearest beneficiary of the planned curbs on new Chinese transceivers, which Reuters says will go ahead despite Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta lobbying (+9% on Nov 17); execution and capacity to fill the gap are the open questions.
views.GLW: Fiber is installed on site with no absorption, so Corning sees delays almost one for one, but its multi-year hyperscaler contracts (Meta, others) set minimum volumes, and US curbs on Chinese optical gear (+3.5% on Nov 17) favour domestic suppliers.
views.TSM: Wafers and CoWoS are booked a year ahead and re-assigned; record October sales show no sign of US permitting delays reaching the foundry. The new rule narrows foundry and packaging work for designers in restricted countries and SemiAnalysis cut out-year accelerator silicon area 17%, so 2028+ is the risk; the 6.3% drop on Nov 16 was sector-wide, and 2027 is effectively immune.
views.AMAT: Second-order only: fab plans for 2027–28 do not change because one US state pauses data centers. FQ4 revenue was a record $10.41B (+53%), it guided $11.1B for FQ1 and more than 30% wafer-fab equipment growth in 2027 with demand 'much higher than supply', yet the stock fell 2.7% with the chip group, a sentiment move against improving fundamentals.
views.ASML: Least exposed: Samsung and SK hynix are reportedly racing to lock in EUV tools (up to KRW 10–20T each) as lead times stretch, so orders are set by memory and logic capacity plans that are still rising, not by US campus timing.
views.TER: Test volumes follow GPU/HBM unit output, which stays supply-capped, so little impact.
views.VRT: Most directly exposed equipment name: UPS, thermal and liquid cooling ship with construction schedules. Backlog and the shift to friendly states and overseas (Vertiv sells globally) limit lost revenue.
views.ROK: Small AI data center exposure; mostly an industrial cycle story.
views.GEV: Mixed but net winner: grid gear for Texas sites slips, while pay-your-own-power rules push hyperscalers to self-supply with gas turbines, its sold-out product. SoftBank's $3.7B write-off on reserved power equipment for Ohio is a warning that slot reservations can be re-scoped, but GE Vernova says deposits are non-refundable and there is no financial impact, and data centers are only ~20% of its gas customers.
views.BE: Clear second-order winner: Google's $17B Wyoming campus will run mostly on a 702 MW AEP fuel-cell plant built with Bloom cells, and NTT DATA signed for 900 MW more (deliveries from 2027). Pay-your-own-power rules in the Senate bill and state platforms push hyperscalers to behind-the-meter power that deploys in months, while gas turbines are sold out into the 2030s. Nebius said Nov 12 that its Microsoft site in Vineland, New Jersey is switching its main power to Bloom fuel cells after the operator retired temporary generation, another case of fuel cells bridging a stalled grid hook-up.
views.VST: Most exposed power name: its growth thesis is new Texas data center load, and management admits the permit pause is already softening ERCOT prices. Still, Q3 beat, 2027 guidance was set above 2026, and it signed a 207 MW Odessa data center PPA, so the 10.6% Nov 6 bounce reflects earnings resilience rather than reduced Texas risk.
views.CEG: Scarcity winner, now confirmed by results: Q3 beat, guidance raised, and about 8.5 GW of long-term deals signed this year (Amazon, Google) with no cost to existing customers. If new capacity is harder to build, plants already on the grid become more valuable, though PJM ratepayer politics cap upside.

ownerStack.note: Indicative. Supplier mix per company is Claude’s estimate from public chip, networking and power deals; categories not listed use the industry default mix. Impact = the share of a company’s Building + Blocked GW in hostile states that slips in the next 12 months on the impact map’s base case (delayed GW pro rata, less what is rebuilt in friendly states, moved abroad or switched to on-site power) × content per GW × supplier share × (1 − absorption), i.e. the revenue that would slip if those projects were delayed a year after the supply chain re-sells what it can. Planned GW is shown separately as later-dated. Arm is shown at its royalty (~5% of the CPU value); Grace CPUs count as Nvidia.

googl.chips: Mostly TPUs (designed with Broadcom); some Nvidia; Axion (Arm) CPUs

meta.chips: Nvidia, AMD MI-series and MTIA (with Broadcom)

sbank.chips: Nvidia for OpenAI Stargate; OpenAI–Broadcom custom chip later

apld.chips: Nvidia via CoreWeave and hyperscaler tenants

frmi.chips: All AMD Instinct via TensorWave (lease not yet in effect)
